title: Python Core (Beginner to Advanced)
tagline: Master the Python language end-to-end through projects: fundamentals, idiomatic and functional Python, object-oriented design, packaging and environments, the standard library, and concurrency, perfo…
summary: Master the Python language end-to-end through projects: fundamentals, idiomatic and functional Python, object-oriented design, packaging and environments, the standard library, and concurrency, performance, and testing. The language foundation every Python role assumes — and the base the AI/ML, Web, and Data-Automation tracks build on.

capstone.title: Packaged, typed, tested CLI library
capstone.project: Build a useful command-line tool as a properly packaged Python project: type-hinted throughout, tested with pytest (with coverage), documented, and published to TestPyPI so anyone can `pip install` it.

phases.title: Language Fundamentals
phases.goal: Read and write clean, correct Python: types, collections, control flow, functions, and exceptions.

projects.title: Unit Converter CLI
projects.description: Build an interactive command-line unit converter to learn Python's core types, type conversion, functions, conditionals, loops, and exception handling.

projects.title: String Toolkit
projects.description: Build a small library of text utilities (slugify, word count, title-case, reverse, palindrome check) to master Python strings, slicing, methods, and f-string formatting.

projects.title: Number Guessing Game
projects.description: Build a guess-the-number game with hints, attempt limits, and replay to master numbers, the random module, comparison operators, and while loops.

projects.title: To-Do List (Lists & Tuples)
projects.description: Build an in-memory to-do manager with add/list/complete/remove to master Python lists, tuples, indexing, iteration, and mutation vs immutability.

projects.title: Contact Book (Dicts & Sets)
projects.description: Build a searchable contact book to master dictionaries (key/value lookup), sets (uniqueness and membership), and why hashing makes them fast.

projects.title: Data Cleaning with Comprehensions
projects.description: Clean a messy list of records using list, dict, and set comprehensions, learning when a comprehension improves clarity and when it hurts it.

projects.title: Control Flow Patterns
projects.description: Implement classic exercises (FizzBuzz, a multiplication table, a simple text menu with match/case, and prime detection) to master conditionals, loops, and structural pattern matching.

projects.title: Functions Deep Dive
projects.description: Build a small statistics toolkit to master function parameters, default arguments, *args/**kwargs, multiple return values, scope, and the mutable-default-argument trap.

projects.title: Errors & Input Validation
projects.description: Build a reusable validation layer with custom exceptions to master try/except/else/finally, exception hierarchy, raising and chaining, and the EAFP vs LBYL styles.

phases.title: Idiomatic & Functional Python
phases.goal: Write Python the way Python developers do: comprehensions, generators, decorators, typing, and the functional toolkit.

projects.title: Unpacking, Starred Targets & zip
projects.description: Build a CSV row transformer to master tuple/dict unpacking, starred assignment, zip, enumerate, and dict merging — the idioms that make Python code concise.

projects.title: Iterators & Generators
projects.description: Build a lazy log-file reader and number streams using the iterator protocol and generator functions with yield, learning lazy evaluation and memory efficiency.

projects.title: Decorators
projects.description: Build timing, caching, and retry decorators to learn how functions wrap other functions, why functools.wraps matters, and how decorators with arguments work.

projects.title: Closures & Higher-Order Functions
projects.description: Build configurable function factories and pipelines to master closures, functions as values, higher-order functions, and lambda — the foundation under decorators and callbacks.

projects.title: Functional Toolkit: map, filter, reduce, partial
projects.description: Process data with map, filter, functools.reduce, functools.partial, and the operator module — and learn when these beat a comprehension and when they don't.

projects.title: itertools Recipes
projects.description: Solve real problems with itertools (chain, islice, groupby, count, cycle, combinations, permutations, accumulate) to learn efficient, lazy iteration patterns.

projects.title: Type Hints & Static Checking with mypy
projects.description: Add complete type hints to a small module and verify them with mypy: built-in generics, Optional/Union, type aliases, Protocols, and Generics.

projects.title: Dataclasses, Enums & NamedTuples
projects.description: Model structured records with dataclasses (mutable, frozen, with defaults and methods), Enums for fixed choices, and NamedTuple for lightweight immutable records.

phases.title: Object-Oriented Python & Design
phases.goal: Model problems with classes done well — inheritance, dunder methods, properties, ABCs, and Pythonic design.

projects.title: Classes & Instances
projects.description: Model a bank account with classes to learn __init__, instance vs class attributes, methods, and the role of self.

projects.title: Dunder Methods (Operator Overloading)
projects.description: Build a Vector and a Money class implementing __repr__/__str__, __eq__/__hash__, __add__, comparison, and __len__ to learn how Python's data model makes objects behave like built-ins.

projects.title: Inheritance, super() & the MRO
projects.description: Model a shape hierarchy to learn inheritance, method overriding, super(), and how Python resolves methods across multiple base classes (the MRO).

projects.title: Properties & Encapsulation
projects.description: Use @property, setters, and computed attributes to enforce invariants and expose a clean interface, learning Python's convention-based encapsulation.

projects.title: Abstract Base Classes & Interfaces
projects.description: Define a payment-processor interface with abc.ABC and @abstractmethod so subclasses are forced to implement required methods, learning interface-based design.

projects.title: Composition over Inheritance
projects.description: Model a Car built from an Engine, Wheels, and a Logger to learn composition, delegation, and dependency injection — and when they beat inheritance.

projects.title: Class Methods & Static Methods
projects.description: Add alternative constructors and utility methods to a Date/Color class to learn @classmethod, @staticmethod, and how they differ from instance methods.

projects.title: Pythonic Design Patterns
projects.description: Implement Strategy, Factory, and a Pythonic Singleton/registry, learning how Python's first-class functions and modules simplify classic OO patterns.

phases.title: Modules, Packaging & Environments
phases.goal: Turn scripts into installable, reproducible, distributable packages.

projects.title: Modules & the Import System
projects.description: Split a script into multiple modules and learn how Python's import system works: import vs from-import, absolute vs relative imports, __name__, and how sys.path resolves modules.

projects.title: Packages & Project Structure
projects.description: Organize modules into an installable package with a src layout, __init__.py, and a clean public API, learning how real Python projects are structured.

projects.title: Virtual Environments & pip
projects.description: Create isolated environments with venv, install and pin dependencies with pip and requirements.txt, and learn why isolation and reproducibility matter.

projects.title: pyproject.toml & Building a Package
projects.description: Write a pyproject.toml, build a wheel and sdist, and install your package locally (editable) — the modern, standardized way to package Python.

projects.title: Publishing to PyPI (TestPyPI)
projects.description: Publish your package to TestPyPI with twine, then install it back with pip — the full release loop, practiced safely on the test index.

projects.title: Dependency Management & Lockfiles
projects.description: Use a modern tool (uv or Poetry) to resolve, lock, and reproduce dependencies, learning version constraints, lockfiles, and how dependency resolution handles conflicts.

projects.title: CLI Entry Points
projects.description: Turn your package into an installable command-line tool using project.scripts entry points and argparse, so users can run it by name after pip install.

phases.title: Standard Library & I/O
phases.goal: Get real work done with the batteries Python includes: files, data formats, dates, regex, logging, and processes.

projects.title: Files & pathlib
projects.description: Build a file-organizing tool using pathlib to read, write, move, and inspect files and directories the modern way, learning paths, encodings, and safe I/O.

projects.title: Context Managers
projects.description: Write custom context managers with both __enter__/__exit__ and contextlib.contextmanager (a timer, a temporary-directory, a DB-like transaction) to master guaranteed setup/teardown.

projects.title: JSON & CSV Data Formats
projects.description: Read, write, and convert between JSON and CSV with the standard library, handling nested data, types, and the quirks of each format.

projects.title: Dates, Times & Time Zones
projects.description: Build a small scheduling/age calculator to master datetime, timedelta, parsing/formatting, and the critical difference between naive and timezone-aware datetimes.

projects.title: Regular Expressions
projects.description: Build a log/text extractor with the re module: patterns, groups, named groups, substitution, and compiled patterns, learning when regex is the right tool and when it isn't.

projects.title: Logging Done Right
projects.description: Replace print debugging with the logging module: levels, loggers, handlers, formatters, and writing to console and file with structured output.

projects.title: Subprocess & OS Interaction
projects.description: Run external commands with subprocess and interact with the environment via os/shutil, learning safe argument passing, capturing output, exit codes, and avoiding shell-injection.

phases.title: Concurrency, Performance & Testing
phases.goal: Make Python fast, concurrent, and trustworthy — and prove it with tests.

projects.title: Threading & the GIL
projects.description: Speed up I/O-bound work with threads and learn why the GIL means threads help I/O but not CPU-bound code, plus thread safety with locks.

projects.title: Multiprocessing
projects.description: Use multiprocessing to parallelize CPU-bound work across cores, learning processes vs threads, Pool/map, and the cost of inter-process communication.

projects.title: Asyncio Basics
projects.description: Learn async/await, coroutines, and the event loop by building an async program, understanding how single-threaded concurrency handles many I/O operations.

projects.title: Async Concurrency Patterns
projects.description: Build a concurrent async fetcher with tasks, gather, timeouts, semaphores for rate-limiting, and error handling — the patterns real async code uses.

projects.title: concurrent.futures
projects.description: Use ThreadPoolExecutor and ProcessPoolExecutor for a unified, high-level pool API, learning futures, executor.map, as_completed, and choosing the right pool.

projects.title: Profiling & Optimization
projects.description: Measure performance with timeit and cProfile, find the real bottleneck, and optimize it with data-driven changes (better algorithms/data structures, caching), avoiding premature optimization.

projects.title: pytest Basics
projects.description: Write your first automated test suite with pytest: test functions, plain assert, testing for exceptions, and structuring tests so they run from one command.

projects.title: Fixtures & Parametrization
projects.description: Use pytest fixtures for reusable setup/teardown and parametrize to run one test across many inputs, keeping tests DRY and thorough.

projects.title: Mocking & Coverage
projects.description: Isolate external dependencies with unittest.mock (patch, Mock, monkeypatch) and measure test thoroughness with coverage, learning to test code that talks to networks, time, or files.
